s1.syndrome_frame: Persistent vertical misalignment with elevation deficit
salient_findings: Elevation deficit of the right eye
Right orbital linear soft-tissue lesion medial to the medial rectus muscle
History of anomalous band in the right orbit
key_facts: 52-year-old woman
History of long-standing diplopia
Persistent vertical misalignment
Orthotropic in primary position
Elevation deficit of the right eye
Previous MRI of the orbits revealed an anomalous band in the right orbit
Surgical excision of the anomalous band did not improve motility
MRI of the orbits with and without gadolinium showed normal globes
No measured proptosis
Retroocular fat, optic nerves and sheaths, optic chiasm, and brain parenchyma appeared normal
Right orbital linear soft-tissue lesion was noted medial to the medial rectus muscle

differentials: Medullary cystic disease of the extraocular muscles
per_call: Medullary cystic disease of the extraocular muscles

shortlist.label: Adhesive syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: History of surgical excision of an anomalous band and persistent diplopia

shortlist.label: Brown syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Elevation deficit of the right eye and previous anomalous band in the right orbit

shortlist.label: Superior oblique tendon sheath syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Vertical misalignment and orthotropic in primary position

shortlist.label: Monocular elevation deficiency
shortlist.why_kept: Elevation deficit of the right eye

shortlist.label: Thyroid ophthalmopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Orbital soft-tissue lesion with enhancement and signal-intensity characteristics identical to those of extraocular muscle

raw.rationale: The patient's history of an anomalous band in the right orbit and previous surgical excision without improvement in motility, along with the presence of a right orbital linear soft-tissue lesion medial to the medial rectus muscle, suggests a chronic inflammatory or fibrotic process consistent with adhesive syndrome.

rejected.label: Brown syndrome
rejected.why: Typically presents with limited elevation in adduction, not a primary elevation deficit

rejected.label: Superior oblique tendon sheath syndrome
rejected.why: Not supported by the imaging findings

rejected.label: Monocular elevation deficiency
rejected.why: Could be a consideration but the presence of the anomalous band and soft-tissue lesion points more towards an adhesive process

rejected.label: Thyroid ophthalmopathy
rejected.why: No evidence of proptosis, globe involvement, or other characteristic findings
